note: Disagreements and source errors found outside the acceptance scenarios. Each names where it was found. Entries marked 'reported, not re-checked' came from the agent that assembled qa/acceptance on 2026-11-21 and have not been read against the sources a second time.

entries.note: qa/research/guides-digest.md, Proclamations table: it lists Proclamations LIX and CXIV twice and never lists CXX, CLVI, CLXX, CXC or CCXIV, which the Adventurer's Journal PDF prints. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: read the Journal PDF's Proclamations and correct the digest.

qa/research/guides-digest.md calls Journal Entry 40 a 'trapper note'; the Adventurer's Journal PDF's Entry 40 is about kobolds and hobgoblins as breeding material. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: read Entry 40 in the Journal PDF and correct the digest.

qa/research/guides-digest.md quotes 'You have defeated the dreaded bandit gang…' beside Journal Entry 50; the Adventurer's Journal PDF's Entry 50 is the Boss's orders and Norris's reply. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: read Entry 50 in the Journal PDF and correct the digest.

Journal entries: qa/research/guides-digest.md cites 36 of the Journal's 58 entries, and qa/inventory/classic.json says the game's scripts reference 26. The gap is unexplained. To settle: list every journal entry number each script block announces, from the scripts, and compare with both.

Silver dragon: the game's own text says the dragon 'throws a fireball'; the Lee guide says save versus breath weapon or take 11d6. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: trace the dice the game draws for that attack with POR_TRACE_DICE.

The Clue Book contradicts itself: page 34 puts the captive lizardmen on pyramid Level 3 and page 36 on the 'second level'. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: find the encounter's script block and map.
Pyramid maze: the Clue Book splits it west and east; the Lee guide splits it north and south. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: read the map data.
The false Tyranthraxus: the Clue Book lists him under the Inner Tower; the Lee guide puts him in the Hedge Maze. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: find the encounter's script block.
The alarm: the Clue Book says it brings patrols; the Lee guide says it does nothing. Reported, not re-checked. To settle: read what the script does when the alarm flag is set.

Map location numbers: the Clue Book numbers map locations differently from the Lee guide throughout (for example New Phlan 1 to 24 in the Clue Book against 2 to 34 in the Lee guide). Scenarios must cite coordinates, not location numbers.

Two transcriptions of the translation wheel disagree on two words the game never asks for: OPTAWA and 8OASIS (oldgames.sk, used in src/codewheel/wheel.json) against OTTAWA and 80ASIS (Andrew Schultz's replica). The enlarged scan shows a P in the first. To settle: read both words on the scans in por-assets/codewheel at full size.

Best fighter/thief: Clue Book p.53 says 'Dwarves and half-elves make the best fighter/thieves because of their high maximum strength and their high maximum fighter level'; the Lee guide §3.1 says 'a fighter/magic-user/thief is more useful still' and §3.2 makes the thief a male elf. Advice, not a fact about the game: play does not settle it. Found in qa/research/party.md.

Single-class humans: Clue Book p.53 says 'let humans be the single class characters' and 'Human fighters can be the best fighters in the game'; the Lee guide §3.2 has one human, the cleric, and no single-class fighter. Advice, not a fact about the game: play does not settle it. Found in qa/research/party.md.

High ability scores and encounter size: Clue Book p.54 says 'Beginning characters with very high ability scores look to the computer like high level adventurers. This may put them at a disadvantage'; the Lee guide §3.1 says to maximize every score with Modify, and its Party Strength (§7.14) counts class levels, armor class, THAC0 and current hit points, not the scores. To settle: compare the size of the Slums' random encounters for the ready-made party and for the guide's party. Found in qa/research/party.md.

When Modify stops: Clue Book p.54 says a character's scores can be modified 'but not after he has gone up a level'; the rule book p.7 says 'The character must start at 0 XP'; the Lee guide (digest section 4) says Modify is allowed while the character has 0 XP. To settle: try Modify Character at a training hall on a character who has experience points and has not trained. Found in qa/research/party.md.

A wrong answer: fan sources (oldgames.sk, dosdays.co.uk, Wikipedia) say the unpatched game allows three tries and then exits to DOS with 'Sorry, that's incorrect', and that START STING skips the check. Not tested: the version 1.3 program GOG sells has the check patched out. To settle: read the code after the comparison in overlay slice 2 of the first release.
